## 債市主線

10月19日科技股回升，避險需求隨之降溫，加上企業重返發債市場、法國公債重挫推升全球殖利率，美國公債下跌。10年期殖利率上升6.69個基點至5.1397%，2年期上升6.36個基點至4.7719%。10年期殖利率的升幅主要來自實質殖利率，先前資金撤出人工智慧投資時帶來的實質借款成本下降，因而部分逆轉。

風險偏好回升並未全面擴散。半導體股上漲1.61%，高評級公司債利差卻小幅擴大，儘管Walmart與Kimberly-Clark的大額新債仍吸引買盤；美國高收益債利差則小幅收窄。曼哈頓一筆辦公大樓證券化交易新近延後，顯示部分不動產借款人取得融資的難度，仍高於成熟的消費企業。

經濟消息也未讓各國央行面臨一致的政策方向。美國建商信心降至14年低點，反映高昂房貸成本的傷害。加拿大通膨低於預期，但其後公布的通膨預期上升、企業準備漲價，又強化加拿大央行升息押注。中國成長優於預期，並勾勒貨幣政策架構的重大調整；印尼股市的信心衝擊，則進一步波及公債與匯率。

## 房市疲弱仍難阻美債再遭拋售

週一Nasdaq 100上漲1.17%、S&P 500上漲0.41%，美國公債同步下跌。晶片股在長時間下挫後反彈，降低投資人為防範AI引發股市修正而買進公債的即時需求。VIX下跌7.75%至18.44，但過去一週仍上升逾21%。

道明證券Gennadiy Goldberg表示，近期賣壓與反彈交替出現後，市場部位仍脆弱，投資人觀望放大了每日波動。他也指出，新公司債分散了資金需求，包括Walmart意外重返市場，以及Kimberly-Clark為收購籌資。

賣壓集中在中天期，而非所有長天期借款的溢價一致上升。5年期美債殖利率上升7.16個基點至4.9399%，30年期僅上升4.64個基點至5.4673%。2年與10年期利差幾乎不變，擴大0.33個基點至36.78個基點；較長端曲線則趨平，2年與30年期利差收窄1.72個基點至69.54個基點。

本次殖利率反彈僅部分抵銷前一波債市漲勢。過去一週，10年與30年期殖利率仍分別下降9.81與12.83個基點，2年期僅下降1.5個基點；但過去一個月，10年與30年期仍分別上升14.27與14.03個基點。近期防禦性買盤的支撐尚未完全消退，較長時間尺度下借款成本上升的壓力也仍存在。

10年期實質殖利率上升6.1個基點至2.783%，解釋了名目殖利率的大部分升幅；損益兩平通膨率僅微升0.59個基點至2.3567%。過去一週，實質殖利率下降10.21個基點，通膨補償則增加0.4個基點。因此週一主要是實質利率壓力重現，長期通膨補償並未大幅重新定價。

油價仍是重要疑慮，但兩大基準走勢分歧。WTI上漲2.23%至每桶$103.67，過去一週上漲10.59%；Brent下跌0.53%至$109.28，過去一個月仍上漲10.06%。實質殖利率上升也壓抑黃金，黃金期貨下跌0.61%至每盎司$4,155.80。美元指數上漲0.13%至101.973。

Bloomberg報導，交易員重新增加對聯準會明年升息的預期，同時仍將12月再升息25個基點納入定價；其美債報導指出，週一交易期間，10月28日升息機率約為20%。瑞銀將年底10年期美債殖利率預測上調至5.2%，理由是聯準會政策路徑更偏鷹、通膨短期改善有限，以及假設油價走勢更高。

新公布的美國房市數據則顯示經濟活動承壓。10月NAHB／Wells Fargo房屋市場指數下降3點至29，為2012年6月以來最低。Bloomberg經濟學家調查預估31，Trading Economics共識為32，前值也是32，實際結果低於兩者預期。

調查各項指標普遍疲弱。目前銷售指數降至33，同為14年低點，未來六個月銷售預期降至2022年11月以來最低，潛在買家來客量則降至疫情爆發以來最低。南部信心為2012年中以來最弱，西部指數下跌10點至2011年底以來最低；中西部也轉弱，東北部則改善。

建商已透過降價與優惠因應：43%表示降價，約三分之二提供促銷誘因。房貸利率高於7%、勞工短缺及營建成本偏高，同時擠壓購屋負擔能力與建商利潤。NAHB首席經濟學家Robert Dietz表示，需求仍在，但融資成本、營建費用及消費者信心轉弱，使買家繼續觀望。利率敏感產業已受到緊縮約束，債市卻重新反映進一步升息。

## 法債賣壓與加拿大調查加重政策壓力

週末因生活成本引發的抗議演變為暴力事件，投資人重新評估法國財政整頓的政治難度，法債領跌歐洲市場。依Bloomberg美債報導，法國10年期殖利率盤中上升約14個基點至接近4.95%，為2002年以來最高。

較早的歐洲市場觀察顯示，法國相對德國的殖利率溢價擴大8個基點至146個基點，創兩週高點，與義大利殖利率的差距也達紀錄水準。原本爭議不斷的預算協商因此承受更迫切的市場壓力：恢復秩序、回應家庭負擔，與政府減少借款的目標互相牽制。

目前提出的2027年預算包含€430億減赤措施，週一的新一波賣壓正是在這套方案下出現。國會分裂、距總統大選僅六個月，都增加達成協議的難度。德國商業銀行Erik Liem表示，生活成本抗議升級，正擴大政治兩極之間的分歧，可能使預算討論陷入僵局。穆迪將於週五進行評等審查，法國在此之前又面臨新的市場壓力。

英國投資人對財政大臣John Healey的10月28日預算案，則抱持不同期待。M&G、Ninety One、Mediolanum International Funds及Raymond James Wealth Management已在預算公布前買進英國公債，預期政府堅守財政紀律可帶動殖利率下降。瑞銀策略師估計，若預算順利推進，10年期殖利率最多可能下降20個基點。

不過，這些買盤仍未讓英國公債避開當日全球跌勢。歐洲早盤報導顯示，英國10年期殖利率大致持平於5.38%；Bloomberg較晚的美國市場綜述則報為上升6個基點至5.43%，同一份報導中的德國10年期殖利率上升3個基點至3.46%。全球利率走高之際，英國財政帶來的利多仍是未來期待。

Legal & General的Chris Jeffery認為，英國允許為投資舉債、但要求淨金融負債在滾動三年預測期間下降的規則，構成實質約束。Ninety One的Jason Borbora-Sheen因看到政策回歸正統的跡象，已增持較長天期英國公債。Franklin Templeton的David Zahn則較不信服，認為執政黨缺乏削減福利的意願，政府只是在爭取時間。分歧在於預算能否帶來持久調整，而不只是官員重申規則。

新公布的家庭研究也顯示高利率代價。Hamptons發現，9月英國首次購屋者中，56%的房貸支出高於原先租金，為至少十年來最高，平均每月多付£39；40多歲購屋者的比例更達67%，反映其購屋面積較大、房貸期限較短。Moneyfacts指出，本月平均五年固定房貸利率為6%，約三年來最高。即使租金已昂貴，家庭離開租屋市場後可獲得的財務紓解，仍受融資負擔限制。

德國央行週一報告對通膨衝擊作了更細緻的區分。報告認為風險明顯偏向上行，來源包括大宗商品，以及食品、非能源商品與服務成本可能上升；但不太可能重演2021至2022年的情況。此次衝擊較集中於石油與成品油，需求及勞動市場較弱，也降低企業頻繁調價或積極轉嫁成本的能力。市場預期ECB於12月升息至2.75%，通膨上行風險仍在，但成本向售價傳導的力道較弱。

加拿大週一的消息則顯示，對成本傳導的判斷可以在一個交易日內迅速改變。9月CPI年增3.1%，高於8月的3%，但低於Bloomberg共識3.2%；月增0.1%。汽油通膨從22.8%加速至27.8%，央行採用的核心通膨中位數與截尾平均指標卻分別降至1.9%與1.8%，剔除食品與能源的通膨維持2.1%。

價格上漲的廣度起初支持耐心觀望。CPI項目中漲幅至少3%的占比，由34.2%降至29.2%；食品雜貨通膨從2.8%降至1.7%，為2024年5月以來最低。居住通膨則受燃料、保險、保養與維修成本影響，從1.5%升至1.8%。道明經濟學家Leslie Preston認為，幾乎看不到高能源價格已廣泛擴散的證據；CIBC的Andrew Grantham則認為，決策官員仍有時間評估關稅及美加貿易關係。

加拿大央行當天稍晚公布企業與消費者調查後，焦點從已實現價格轉向未來漲價。家庭長期通膨預期上升，約半數企業計畫將能源與關稅增加的部分或全部成本轉嫁出去。多數回覆收集於美國貿易談判破裂之前，之後收集的回覆則顯示關稅壓抑企業展望。

BMO、RBC及Desjardins改為預測10月28日升息，將政策利率提高至2.5%；Scotiabank強化原有升息預測，Manulife仍預期本月與12月都升息。渥太華當天下午稍晚，隔夜交換反映10月升息機率達80%，高於週一稍早的近70%，及一週前約30%。加拿大各天期公債均遭拋售，未因CPI低於預期而獲支撐；近期Bloomberg經濟學家調查則仍以維持利率不變為主流。

Desjardins的Royce Mendes表示，投入成本長期居高不下，已預示消費者物價將更廣泛上漲。總裁Tiff Macklem週末也表示，高油價除了推升通膨，還支持出口、所得、政府收入與投資。但勞動市場依然脆弱，就業人數自12月以來已減少41,200人。調查使未來通膨的政策回應更顯迫切，卻未消除貿易對經濟活動的拖累。

## 中國調整利率架構，亞洲風險走向分歧

中國第三季GDP年增率由第二季4.3%加速至4.5%，優於預期，帶動前三季成長4.6%，落在北京全年4.5%至5%的目標範圍。9月工業生產成長5.5%，為六個月最快；零售銷售成長1.1%，為3月以來最強、逾預測增速兩倍，但生產與家庭需求的落差仍明顯。

部分消費細節比總數更佳。剔除汽車後，零售銷售成長3.9%，為2025年10月以來最快，受惠於通訊設備、食品、菸酒；汽車補貼縮減後，購車持續萎縮。價格上漲加快、假期時間提前，也推升名目銷售，使改善幅度不能全數視為實際銷售量增強。

前三季房地產投資下降20.6%，拖累固定資產投資下降7.2%。9月城鎮調查失業率由5.3%改善至5.2%，但房市長期低迷，持續限制工廠轉強對整體經濟的帶動。為抵銷民間支出疲弱，官方加大公共投資，第三季用於投資的地方專項債發行，加速至至少2025年初以來最快。

美國銀行Helen Qiao預期，隨著目標已可望達成，政策支持大致維持目前力道，只作邊際調整。澳盛銀行邢兆鵬則強調，財政擴張能在多大程度上支持復甦延續至2027年，仍不確定。GDP優於預期，降低了立即推出更大刺激方案的壓力，內需失衡卻未改變。

中國人民銀行行長潘功勝另在北京金融街論壇提出貨幣政策重大調整：將研究在適當時機，把公開市場操作主要期限由7天改為隔夜，屆時隔夜逆回購利率將成為主要政策工具。他表示，交易活躍的銀行間隔夜回購利率DR001，已是人行操作的目標。

這項改變除簡化架構，也可能降低借款成本。6月推出的新隔夜逆回購交易定價為1.25%；張繼強領導的華泰證券分析師先前認為，改採較低的隔夜基準相當於實質寬鬆。澳盛邢兆鵬表示，若新政策利率低於1.4%，利率走廊須重新調整，但最終利率水準尚未確定。

消息未立即引發明顯債市重新定價。銀行間隔夜回購利率持穩於1.26%，10年及30年期公債殖利率也大致持平於1.64%及2.06%。該則報導中的離岸人民幣維持稍早漲幅，升值0.1%至每美元6.6813元。

潘功勝也提議調整貸款及金融商品的參考利率。體質較佳企業可協商與銀行間隔夜回購利率連動的貸款，貸款市場報價利率LPR則可繼續適用於小企業與個人。債券及衍生商品也可參考回購利率，後續將提供指引。隨LPR對市場狀況的反應變弱，已有數家銀行自7月開始試行與銀行間利率連動的放款。

另一項新的流動性工具，則針對非銀行機構面臨大額贖回的需要。人行將與金融及證券監管機關合作建立機制，避免債券拋售與流動性短缺互相強化。這是與流動性價格架構調整並行、但目的不同的穩定措施。

印尼面臨更急迫的資金外流問題。MSCI威脅將印尼由新興市場降為獨立市場後，雅加達綜合指數延續週五重挫，週一盤中最多再跌5.4%。10年期公債殖利率跳升12個基點，一度達7.47%，印尼盾貶值0.2%；5年期走勢不同，週五飆升22個基點後，週一最多下降11個基點。

當局將個股單日跌幅上限由15%縮至7%，實施至年底，官員並計畫向MSCI尋求釐清。高盛估計，若完全移出MSCI基準，可能帶來約$56億被動資金外流；若富時羅素跟進，另有$27億面臨風險。未來資產估計約$30億，花旗則估計為數十億美元區間的中段。這些是未來可能重新分類造成的外流估算，今年已發生的外資股票撤資則為$51億。

企業也宣布庫藏股計畫：與Prajogo Pangestu有關的三家公司合計規劃2.5兆印尼盾，Dian Swastatika Sentosa另提出1兆印尼盾。SEB的Eugenia Victorino與MUFG的Lloyd Chan指出，匯率轉弱進一步降低外資持有印尼債券的意願。星展警告，若修正擴大，10年期殖利率可能升向7.5%，並促使印尼央行再升息50至100個基點。

日本新的政策溝通則針對另一類主權市場疑慮。首相高市早苗否認日圓疲弱與高利率是其政策造成，並承諾在下年度預算中妥善控制日本公債發行。與她一同出席國會的日本央行總裁植田和男表示，基礎通膨正接近2%，並警告若市場認為政策利率調升過慢，長期殖利率可能上升。他的說明讓貨幣政策正常化步調，與政府的財政保證並列為市場關注。

澳洲央行助理總裁Christopher Kent對進一步緊縮則較謹慎。他表示，部分勞動指標鬆動速度快於預測，但尚難區分是需求減弱，還是勞動成本上升所致。他認為現金利率及其預期路徑，已接近央行中性利率估計的上緣，因此對政策具有緊縮性有一定信心；是否足夠緊縮，仍須在11月更新預測時，結合勞動市場證據與即將公布的通膨資料判斷。

## 大型發行人順利籌資，不動產交易受阻

週一四家公司合計發行$104億美國投資等級公司債。Kimberly-Clark為尚待完成的Kenvue收購案，完成五批、期限介於2年至10年的$49億發債；最長天期券定價為美債加72個基點，初步討論約為加100個基點。繼週五舉行投資人電話會議後，這筆融資已完成定價，籌資條件也隨之明朗。

Walmart完成$30億美元債定價，期限3年至10年，最高認購需求逾$140億；10年期券利差為美債加45個基點。公司另啟動首次加幣發債，規模C$50億，使兩筆發行的預計總值約達$65億。

隨投資計畫擴大，加幣發債有助Walmart拓展投資人基礎與融資幣別。分析師預期，公司明年資本支出將創紀錄達$290億，2027年另有約$33億債券到期。Walmart已於4月在美國募得$42.5億，此次重返市場打破慣常每年發債一次的模式。加拿大投資人買進海外發行人，以分散產業與公司曝險，借款人也因此增加融資管道。

大型發行順利，並未阻止投資等級利差小幅擴大。LQD單日總報酬為負0.50%，HYG則下跌0.04%，同期高收益債利差小幅收窄；EMB報酬為負0.47%。即使信用風險溢價較有韌性，公債殖利率走高仍壓抑報酬。

不動產擔保債務籌資則更困難。信用條件轉弱、利率波動之際，曼哈頓475 Fifth Avenue抵押貸款的$1.75億證券化案延後；其中$7,412萬AAA級券先前以基準加約180個基點行銷，原預計10月6日定價。這棟24層大樓是Penske Media美東總部，截至9月1日出租率93.4%，但即使有此出租率，投資人提供融資的意願仍受限。

摩根士丹利也難以為一批與堪薩斯市資料中心連結、約$3.01億的抵押貸款債券吸引需求。繼先前住宅及商用不動產發行延後後，曼哈頓新一筆延案與資料中心行銷困難，顯示融資壓力擴散，但大型無擔保公司債仍可完成交易。

另一些借款人透過調整資產負債結構，而非僅靠發債籌資。Primary Health Properties與GIC成立£7億醫院合資事業，初始納入27家私立醫院。PHP將取得約£5億，用於償還收購Assura的過橋貸款及另一項融資，使淨負債降至約£29億。這項安排在降低負債的同時，保留醫療不動產曝險，並引入新資本夥伴。

Silgan同意以$34億企業價值收購Trivium Packaging，並將其與旗下金屬容器及食品飲料平蓋業務合併。American Industrial Partners將投資約$10億，取得合併單位40%股權，其餘由Silgan持有。Silgan預期透過合併取得約$23億現金，用於償債，因此股權重組是本次收購融資效果的關鍵。

CIBC正準備發行C$7.5億至C$10億額外第一類資本有限追索權資本票據，初步討論為政府基準加約300個基點。證券期限約60年，五年後可贖回，遇財務困境時可轉為股權。Optiver則尋求約$7億債務與$2億循環額度以擴大交易。知情人士表示，市場不確定性與美國期中選舉使時程未定，融資計畫仍可能取消。

市政融資持續支應個別擴建計畫。The Villages擬發行近$1.8億未評等高收益債，預計10月20日定價，用於3,860戶住宅及設施，包括27洞錦標賽級高爾夫球場。這項約6,670戶擴建案的第一期，去年已借入約$1.27億。

Las Vegas Valley Water District本週計畫發行約$5.8億免稅債，用於基礎建設與再融資；工程包括Apex Industrial Park供水、Henderson管線，以及參與南加州水回收。標普給予AA+評等，理由是用戶成長之際，節水措施與儲備水量仍有成效。該水務機構也正就聯邦政策提告，因最嚴峻情況下，內華達州科羅拉多河配水量可能被削減達70%；該河供應河谷約90%的用水。

美國銀行Kay Hope對非洲企業融資提出新評估。前三季硬通貨發債達$133億，其中私募$32.5億，為2021年全年$170億以來最快的發行步調。發行人來自11國，2021年為八國。Hope指出，評等調升多於調降，且該領域自2020年以來無付款違約，但仍提醒主權壓力可能傳至企業。

未來到期規模使融資管道能否持續暢通格外重要。United Bank for Africa下月有$3億到期，2027年四家發行人合計$22億，2028年九家近$70億；後者包括Eskom的$15億、Tullow Oil的$12億及Transnet的$10億。Hope預期年度供給為$80億至$120億，但高利率可能使部分再融資轉向本地市場、貸款或海灣資金。

## AI融資爭議聚焦合約報酬與資金需求

即使獲高盛調升評等，CoreWeave仍未守住週一早盤股價漲勢。股價一度上漲7.4%，隨後短暫跌逾2%，終場下跌0.4%。分析師Gabriela Borges將評等升至買進，但目標價由$139降至$106，承認下一階段融資的可得性與成本仍不確定。

Borges估計，CoreWeave綜合債務成本可能上升100至200個基點，但大概不會更多；依高盛評估，股權報酬仍具吸引力。她預期未來24個月運算供給吃緊，加上CoreWeave的效能與落實計畫能力優勢，將支撐專案報酬。

摩根大通週五完成、週一見報的分析，從合約提供更具體的反論。Samik Chatterjee等分析師估計，典型五年合約的未槓桿內部報酬率，約為15%，高於估計9%至11%的綜合資金成本。照付不議承諾讓產能投運前就有客戶保障，首個五年期結束後，GPU若再出租還可能帶來額外收入。

該行保守情境估計，資本支出約占合約價值51%，其中約80%由資產層級債務融資。償還債務後，可能剩餘相當於合約價值約16%的現金；即使客戶不續約，在其模型中也足以支應約五年的資料中心付款義務。這個比例的分母是合約價值，並非CoreWeave公司債持有人的預估回收率。

同一分析也說明，專案報酬良好，為何仍伴隨巨額融資需求。每1吉瓦全面運轉的產能，每年可創造$100億至$150億營收，但新增這些產能須先投入逾$350億。摩根大通估計，要到2030年，既有營運才可能足以支應擴張，屆時已投入營運產能可能達每年新增產能的四至五倍。因此，能產生現金的產能與在建規模之間的比例，決定外部融資需求將持續多久。

Nscale則為這場爭論帶來潛在需求承諾。這家獲Nvidia支持的開發商，正與Anthropic洽談可能近$450億的運算供應協議，涉及西維吉尼亞州一座新中心的460 MW產能，採用Nvidia Vera Rubin晶片。同時，投資人質疑其IPO尋求的約$300億估值，部分人認為$160億至$190億較能吸引支持。潛在客戶訂單與股權估值阻力，反映同一融資挑戰的不同面向。

GTCR的Nelson Iginla則從軟體收購融資提供另一觀察。他表示，CCC Intelligent Solutions業務品質佳，使貸款人願為收購案提供強力融資方案；其專有資料，以及串聯保險公司、維修廠與其他參與者的網路，使服務難以複製。但GTCR也研究過AI已侵蝕財務表現的企業。他強調的是個別公司的韌性，而非整個軟體業融資意願普遍恢復。

IMF新研究把AI討論從資本支出延伸至就業。一份涵蓋110個經濟體、逾7億筆線上職缺的工作論文發現，自2022年底ChatGPT推出後，受AI影響產業的招募已減少近10%；隨企業增加對能運用AI人員的需求，降幅正逐漸趨穩。大型企業較常要求這類技能，但即使在這群企業中，看來將其列為必要條件的比例仍不到20%。

潘功勝則提出貨幣政策面臨的時間先後問題：AI短期可能推升投資與通膨，中長期才提高生產力、抑制物價漲幅。他表示，整體就業尚未受顯著影響，但工作結構正在改變。他對整體就業的評估，與IMF對特定受影響產業的發現，衡量的是不同層面的調整；工作遭取代之際，新的招募機會也開始出現。

## 後續市場觀察

10月20日美國房市資料，將讓實際營建與交易活動，對照建商信心惡化情況。9月新屋開工預估131萬戶，前值127.5萬戶；建照初值預估140萬戶，前值140.3萬戶。成屋待完成銷售預估月減0.5%，前值月增0.3%。若開工回升、交易仍弱，建商面臨的庫存與現金流問題，將不同於兩者同時萎縮。

週度ADP就業變動於週二公布，接著是週三房貸申請及週四首次申請失業救濟人數。週五10月S&P Global製造業與服務業PMI初值，將提供更廣泛的活動比較：共識分別為55.5與57.9，前值為55.9與58.8。同日密西根大學終值，預估五年通膨預期為3.5%。這組資料將反映高融資成本是否正壓抑需求，而通膨預期依舊難以控制。

美國財政部10月21日20年期公債、10月22日5年期TIPS標售，將在週一實質殖利率上升後，檢驗長天期名目債券及通膨保障的需求。大型企業也在籌資之際，重點是較高殖利率能吸引多少投資人承接利率曝險。

法國週五迎來穆迪審查，目前殖利率溢價更高，政治上對財政調整的抵抗仍在。英國週三公布9月通膨，預測為3.4%，隨後是10月28日預算案及11月英國央行可能升息。加拿大10月28日決策，則面對核心物價趨緩與調查顯示未來成本轉嫁之間更鮮明的分歧，數家大銀行已改為預測升息。

印尼央行週三決策前，股票、公債與印尼盾又一波下跌，穩定市場與因應潛在指數資金外流，成為迫切政策議題。日本週五通膨及澳洲即將公布的通膨資料，將有助判斷兩國官員分別強調政策正常化及勞動市場降溫的立場是否延續。

Meta與Tesla週三財報，將檢驗週一科技股反彈背後的營運假設。對AI債權人而言，需求轉為營收、建設支出及新融資成本相互關聯，卻是不同問題。Nscale的協商與擬議IPO，將顯示大額潛在客戶承諾能否換得可接受的融資條件；CoreWeave產能提升進度，則持續決定其對外部資金的依賴。中國承諾提供的貸款與債券基準指引，將另行釐清擬議隔夜政策架構如何傳入實際融資合約。

overall_summary.headline: 科技股反彈、企業發債回流與法債重挫，帶動美債下跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
10月19日科技股回升，避險需求降溫，加上企業重返發債市場及法債下跌推升全球殖利率，美國公債走低。10年期美債殖利率上升6.69個基點至5.1397%，其中實質殖利率上升6.1個基點至2.783%，損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.59個基點至2.3567%。2年期殖利率上升6.36個基點至4.7719%，中天期賣壓較最長端更重。這次反轉僅部分抵銷先前漲勢，10年期殖利率過去一週仍下降9.81個基點。

Nasdaq 100回升1.17%，但融資市場並未全面受惠於風險偏好改善。Walmart與Kimberly-Clark完成大額美元債發行，美國投資等級債利差卻小幅擴大，高收益債利差則小幅收窄。曼哈頓一筆$1.75億辦公大樓證券化交易延後。昂貴的房貸與營建成本壓抑需求，建商信心降至29，為2012年6月以來最低。

法國因生活成本引發的暴力抗議，加劇財政緊張；週五穆迪審查前，10年期法債殖利率盤中上升約14個基點至近4.95%。加拿大CPI低於預期，但隨後通膨預期上升、企業準備漲價，引發疑慮，強化10月升息押注並使債券下跌。中國成長轉強，並提出隔夜政策利率架構；印尼可能遭指數重新分類的威脅，則波及公債與印尼盾。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries fell on October 19 as a recovery in technology shares reduced demand for safety, corporate borrowers returned to the market and a sharp selloff in French debt added to pressure on global yields. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 6.69 basis points to 5.1397%, while the two-year increased 6.36 basis points to 4.7719%. Most of the 10-year move came from higher real yields, reversing part of the relief in inflation-adjusted borrowing costs that had accompanied the retreat from artificial-intelligence investments.

The recovery in risk appetite was selective. Semiconductor shares gained 1.61%, but high-grade corporate spreads widened modestly even as Walmart and Kimberly-Clark found buyers for large new offerings. U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly. A newly postponed Manhattan office securitization showed that access to financing remained more difficult for some property borrowers than for established consumer companies.

The day's economic news supplied competing pressures rather than a common direction for central banks. U.S. homebuilder confidence fell to a 14-year low, exposing the damage from expensive mortgages. Canadian inflation undershot expectations, only for rising inflation expectations and planned corporate price increases to strengthen bets on a Bank of Canada hike. China delivered a better growth reading and outlined a major change to its monetary-policy framework, while Indonesia's equity-market confidence shock spread further into government debt and the currency.

## Treasury Selling Resumes Despite Housing Weakness

Monday's Treasury losses accompanied a 1.17% rise in the Nasdaq 100 and a 0.41% gain in the S&P 500. Chipmakers recovered after a prolonged slide, reducing the immediate demand for government bonds as protection against an AI-led equity correction. The VIX fell 7.75% to 18.44, although it remained more than 21% higher over the week.

TD Securities' Gennadiy Goldberg described positioning as fragile after the recent alternation between selling and rallies. Investors staying away were amplifying daily moves, he said. He also identified competing demand from new corporate debt, including Walmart's unexpected return to the market and Kimberly-Clark's acquisition financing.

The five-year Treasury yield rose 7.16 basis points to 4.9399%, while the 30-year increased a smaller 4.64 basis points to 5.4673%. The 2s10s spread was almost unchanged, widening 0.33 basis point to 36.78. The longer curve flattened: 2s30s narrowed 1.72 basis points to 69.54. Selling was therefore stronger in intermediate maturities than at the very long end, rather than a uniform increase in the premium for lending over longer periods.

The rebound in yields only partly reversed the preceding recovery. Ten-year yields remained 9.81 basis points lower over the week and 30-year yields 12.83 basis points lower, compared with a decline of just 1.5 basis points at two years. Over the month, however, the 10-year was still up 14.27 basis points and the 30-year 14.03. The market retained both the recent benefit of defensive demand and the larger increase in borrowing costs over a longer horizon.

At 10 years, the real yield rose 6.1 basis points to 2.783%, accounting for most of the nominal increase. Breakeven inflation edged up 0.59 basis point to 2.3567%. Over the week, the real yield was down 10.21 basis points, while inflation compensation was up 0.4 basis point. Monday's reversal thus principally restored real-rate pressure rather than producing a large new repricing of long-term inflation compensation.

Oil remained an important source of concern, although the benchmarks diverged. WTI rose 2.23% to $103.67 a barrel and was 10.59% higher over the week. Brent slipped 0.53% to $109.28, still up 10.06% over the month. Higher real yields also weighed on gold futures, which fell 0.61% to $4,155.80 an ounce. The Dollar Index rose 0.13% to 101.973.

Traders rebuilt expectations for Fed increases next year while continuing to price another quarter-point move in December, Bloomberg reported. Its Treasury account put the probability of an October 28 increase around 20% during Monday trading. UBS raised its year-end 10-year yield forecast to 5.2%, citing a more hawkish Fed path, limited near-term progress on inflation and a higher assumed oil-price trajectory.

The fresh U.S. housing release pointed in the other direction for activity. The NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index fell 3 points to 29 in October, its lowest since June 2012. Bloomberg's economist survey had expected 31; the Trading Economics consensus was 32. Both placed the outcome below expectations, with the previous reading at 32.

Weakness extended across the survey. Current sales fell to 33, also a 14-year low, while expectations for sales over the next six months reached their weakest level since November 2022. Prospective buyer traffic dropped to its lowest since the onset of the pandemic. Confidence in the South was the weakest since mid-2012, and the West's index fell 10 points to its lowest since late 2011. The Midwest also weakened, while the Northeast improved.

Builders were responding with concessions: 43% reported cutting prices, and about two-thirds were offering incentives. Mortgage rates above 7%, labor shortages and elevated construction costs were squeezing both affordability and margins. NAHB chief economist Robert Dietz said demand persisted, but financing costs, construction expenses and weaker consumer confidence were keeping buyers on the sidelines. The release showed restraint already reaching a rate-sensitive sector even as the bond market returned to pricing further policy tightening.

## France's Selloff and Canada's Surveys Raise Policy Stakes

French bonds led European losses as investors reassessed the political difficulty of fiscal consolidation following the weekend's violent cost-of-living protests. During the session, the French 10-year yield climbed about 14 basis points to nearly 4.95%, its highest since 2002, according to Bloomberg's Treasury account.

An earlier European observation put the French premium over Germany 8 basis points wider at 146 basis points, a two-week high. The gap to Italian yields reached a record. The deterioration turned an already contentious budget negotiation into a more immediate market problem: restoring order and responding to household pressure compete with the government's effort to reduce borrowing.

The current proposed 2027 budget contains EUR43 billion of deficit-reduction measures. That is the fiscal program against which Monday's new selling occurred, with a divided parliament and a presidential election six months away complicating agreement. Commerzbank's Erik Liem said escalating living-cost protests were widening the divide between political extremes and could leave budget discussions in limbo. The new pressure comes ahead of Friday's Moody's review.

Britain attracted a different response from investors looking toward Chancellor John Healey's October 28 budget. M&G, Ninety One, Mediolanum International Funds and Raymond James Wealth Management have bought gilts ahead of the event, anticipating that adherence to fiscal discipline could bring yields down. UBS strategists estimate the 10-year yield could fall by as much as 20 basis points if the budget proceeds smoothly.

That positioning was not enough to insulate gilts from the broader day's losses. An early European account found the UK 10-year little changed at 5.38%; Bloomberg's later U.S. market summary put it 6 basis points higher at 5.43%. German 10-year yields were 3 basis points higher at 3.46% in the same later account. The hoped-for British fiscal relief remained prospective as global rates rose.

Legal & General's Chris Jeffery sees a meaningful constraint in Britain's rules allowing borrowing for investment while requiring net financial debt to fall over a rolling three-year forecast. Ninety One's Jason Borbora-Sheen has added longer gilts, citing signs of policy orthodoxy. Franklin Templeton's David Zahn is less persuaded, arguing that the government is buying time because its party has little appetite for welfare cuts. The disagreement concerns whether the budget can deliver durable adjustment, not merely whether officials reaffirm the rules.

New household research showed how costly the interest-rate backdrop has become. Hamptons found that 56% of first-time UK buyers in September faced mortgage payments above their previous rent, the largest share in at least a decade, with an average increase of GBP39 a month. Among buyers in their 40s, the share reached 67%, reflecting larger homes and shorter mortgage terms. Moneyfacts put the average five-year fixed mortgage rate at 6% this month, its highest in about three years. The financing burden limits how much relief households can get from moving out of an already expensive rental market.

Germany's Bundesbank supplied a more discriminating assessment of the inflation shock. In a Monday report, it said risks were clearly skewed upward, identifying commodities and possible increases in food, non-energy goods and services costs. But it considered a repeat of 2021-22 unlikely. The current shock is more concentrated in oil and refined products, while weaker demand and labor markets reduce companies' ability to increase prices frequently or pass through costs aggressively. The expected December ECB increase to 2.75% sits alongside that distinction between persistent upside risk and a less powerful propagation mechanism.

Canada demonstrated how quickly that propagation assessment can change within a session. September CPI rose 3.1% from a year earlier, up from 3% in August but below Bloomberg's 3.2% consensus. Monthly prices increased 0.1%. Gasoline inflation accelerated to 27.8% from 22.8%, yet the bank's median and trimmed core measures eased to 1.9% and 1.8%, respectively. Inflation excluding food and energy held at 2.1%.

The breadth measures initially favored patience. The share of CPI components rising at least 3% fell to 29.2% from 34.2%. Grocery inflation slowed to 1.7% from 2.8%, the lowest since May 2024. Shelter inflation increased to 1.8% from 1.5%, reflecting fuel, insurance, maintenance and repair costs. TD economist Leslie Preston saw little evidence that expensive energy had spread broadly, while CIBC's Andrew Grantham argued that policymakers had time to assess tariffs and U.S. trade relations.

The Bank of Canada's business and consumer surveys later Monday shifted attention from realized prices to coming increases. Longer-term household inflation expectations rose, and roughly half of firms planned to pass on some or all of the higher costs from energy and tariffs. Most responses preceded the breakdown in U.S. trade talks; those collected afterward showed tariffs weighing on the business outlook.

BMO, RBC and Desjardins changed their forecasts to a hike taking the policy rate to 2.5% on October 28. Scotiabank reinforced its existing hike call, while Manulife continued to expect increases this month and in December. By late afternoon in Ottawa, overnight swaps assigned an 80% probability to an October increase, up from nearly 70% earlier Monday and around 30% a week before. Canadian bonds sold off across the curve despite the softer-than-expected CPI. A recent Bloomberg economist survey still favored a hold.

Desjardins' Royce Mendes said the duration of elevated input costs now pointed toward broader consumer-price increases. Governor Tiff Macklem had also said over the weekend that expensive oil was supporting exports, incomes, government revenue and investment, alongside its inflation effects. That benefit sits against a vulnerable labor market: employment had fallen by 41,200 since December. The surveys made the prospective inflation response more urgent without removing the trade-related drag on activity.

## China Changes Its Rate Framework as Asian Risks Diverge

China's Q3 GDP growth accelerated to 4.5% year on year from 4.3% in Q2, beating expectations and taking growth over the first nine months to 4.6%, inside Beijing's 4.5%-5% annual target. September industrial production rose 5.5%, the fastest in six months. Retail sales increased 1.1%, their strongest growth since March and more than twice the forecast pace, though the gap between production and household demand remained pronounced.

The consumption detail was better than the headline alone suggested in some areas. Excluding cars, retail sales rose 3.9%, the fastest since October 2025, helped by telecommunications equipment, food, tobacco and alcohol. Car purchases continued to contract after subsidies were scaled back. Faster prices and an earlier holiday also lifted nominal sales, limiting how much of the improvement represented stronger underlying volumes.

Property investment fell 20.6% over the first nine months, contributing to a 7.2% decline in fixed-asset investment. The surveyed urban unemployment rate improved to 5.2% in September from 5.3%, but the prolonged housing slump continued to restrict the benefits flowing from stronger factories to the wider economy. Special local-bond issuance for investment accelerated in Q3 to its fastest pace since at least the start of 2025 as officials used public investment to offset weak private spending.

Bank of America's Helen Qiao expects support to remain broadly at its current intensity, with only marginal changes now that the target is within reach. ANZ's Xing Zhaopeng emphasized uncertainty over how much fiscal expansion could sustain the recovery into 2027. The better GDP outcome reduced the immediate pressure for a larger stimulus package while leaving the domestic-demand imbalance intact.

Governor Pan Gongsheng separately outlined a substantial monetary-policy change at Beijing's Financial Street Forum. The PBOC will study moving the main tenor of its open-market operations from seven days to overnight at an appropriate time; the overnight reverse repo rate would then become the principal policy lever. Pan said the heavily traded interbank overnight repo rate, DR001, was already the target of its operations.

The change could lower borrowing costs as well as simplify the framework. New overnight reverse repo transactions were priced at 1.25% when introduced in June. Huatai Securities analysts led by Zhang Jiqiang had argued that switching to the lower overnight benchmark would amount to effective easing. ANZ's Xing said the corridors would need recalibration if the new policy rate were below 1.4%, while the eventual rate level remained unsettled.

There was little immediate bond-market repricing. Overnight interbank repos were steady at 1.26% after the news, while 10- and 30-year government yields were little changed at 1.64% and 2.06%. The offshore yuan retained an earlier gain, up 0.1% at 6.6813 per dollar in that account.

Pan also proposed changing the reference rates used for loans and financial products. Stronger companies could negotiate loans linked to overnight interbank repos, while the loan prime rate could remain relevant for small businesses and individuals. Bonds and derivatives could also reference repos, with guidance to follow. Several banks had begun experimenting with interbank-linked lending in July as the LPR became less responsive to market conditions.

A separate new liquidity facility is intended to help non-bank institutions meet large redemptions. The PBOC will work with financial and securities regulators on a mechanism to prevent bond selling and liquidity shortages from reinforcing each other. That is a distinct stability measure alongside the proposed change in the price of liquidity.

Indonesia faced a more immediate outflow problem. The Jakarta Composite fell as much as 5.4% Monday, extending Friday's rout after MSCI's threat to move the country from emerging-market to standalone status. The 10-year government yield jumped 12 basis points and reached as high as 7.47%, while the rupiah weakened 0.2%. Five-year yields moved differently, falling as much as 11 basis points after a 22-basis-point surge Friday.

Authorities reduced the maximum daily decline for individual shares to 7% from 15% through year-end, and officials planned to seek clarification from MSCI. Goldman Sachs estimated that full removal from MSCI benchmarks could produce about $5.6 billion of passive outflows, with another $2.7 billion at risk if FTSE Russell followed. Mirae Asset's estimate was around $3 billion, while Citi put it in the mid-single-digit billions. These estimates refer to possible future reclassification, against $5.1 billion of foreign equity withdrawals already recorded this year.

Companies also announced buybacks: three linked to Prajogo Pangestu planned a combined 2.5 trillion rupiah, and Dian Swastatika Sentosa proposed another 1 trillion. SEB's Eugenia Victorino and MUFG's Lloyd Chan identified the weaker currency as an additional deterrent for foreign bondholders. DBS warned that a broader correction could push 10-year yields toward 7.5% and lead Bank Indonesia to raise rates by another 50-100 basis points.

Japan's new policy communication addressed a different source of sovereign unease. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi rejected claims that her policies were responsible for the weak yen and high interest rates and promised appropriate control of JGB issuance in next fiscal year's budget. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, appearing with her in parliament, said underlying inflation was approaching 2% and warned that long yields could rise if markets judged policy-rate increases too slow. His explanation placed the pace of monetary normalization beside the government's fiscal assurances.

Australia's Christopher Kent offered a more cautious assessment of further tightening. The RBA assistant governor said some labor indicators were loosening faster than forecast, with the distinction between weaker demand and higher labor costs still unresolved. He regarded the cash rate and its expected path as near the upper end of the bank's neutral estimates, giving some confidence that policy was restrictive. Whether it was restrictive enough would require combining the labor evidence with coming inflation data when forecasts are updated in November.

## Large Issuers Find Buyers While Property Deals Stall

Four companies brought a combined $10.4 billion of U.S. investment-grade bonds Monday. Kimberly-Clark completed $4.9 billion in five tranches spanning two to 10 years for its pending Kenvue acquisition. The longest maturity priced 72 basis points over Treasuries, compared with initial discussions around 100 basis points. The completed financing advanced a transaction that had reached investor calls Friday, replacing uncertainty over execution with actual market terms.

Walmart priced $3 billion of dollar debt with maturities from three to 10 years, attracting more than $14 billion of peak demand. Its 10-year tranche paid 45 basis points over Treasuries. The retailer also launched a C$5 billion Canadian-dollar offering, its first in that currency, bringing the two offerings' expected value to roughly $6.5 billion.

The Canadian sale broadens both the investor base and currency mix as Walmart's investment program expands. Analysts expect capital spending to reach a record $29 billion next year, and about $3.3 billion of bonds mature in 2027. Walmart had already raised $4.25 billion in the U.S. in April, making Monday's return a departure from its usual once-a-year pattern. Canadian investors have been buying foreign issuers to diversify sector and company exposure, while borrowers gain another funding channel.

Those successes coexisted with modestly wider investment-grade spreads. LQD's daily total return was negative 0.50%, compared with a 0.04% decline for HYG as high-yield spreads tightened modestly. EMB returned negative 0.47%. Higher government yields weighed on returns even where credit risk premiums were more resilient.

Property-backed debt faced a harder execution test. A $175 million securitization of the mortgage on Manhattan's 475 Fifth Avenue was postponed amid weaker credit conditions and volatile rates. Its $74.12 million AAA tranche had been marketed around 180 basis points over the benchmark, with pricing initially expected October 6. The 24-story building, Penske Media's East Coast headquarters, was 93.4% occupied as of September 1. Investors' willingness to finance the property remained constrained despite that occupancy.

Morgan Stanley was also struggling to generate demand for roughly $301 million of mortgage bonds tied to a Kansas City data center. The new Manhattan postponement and data-center marketing difficulty extended the financing pressure beyond the previously delayed residential and commercial offerings, without preventing large unsecured corporate deals from completing.

Other borrowers were changing balance-sheet structures rather than relying solely on bond issuance. Primary Health Properties formed a GBP700 million hospital venture with GIC, seeded with 27 private hospitals. PHP will receive about GBP500 million to repay the bridge loan for its Assura acquisition and another facility, reducing net debt to about GBP2.9 billion. The transaction pairs debt reduction with continued exposure to healthcare property and a new capital partner.

Silgan agreed to acquire Trivium Packaging at a $3.4 billion enterprise value and combine it with its metal-container and food-and-beverage flat-cap operations. American Industrial Partners will invest around $1 billion for 40% of the combined unit, with Silgan retaining the rest. Silgan expects about $2.3 billion of cash proceeds from the combination to retire debt, making the ownership reorganization central to the acquisition's financing consequences.

CIBC was preparing C$750 million-C$1 billion of additional tier-one limited recourse capital notes, with initial discussions around 300 basis points above government benchmarks. The approximately 60-year securities would be callable after five years and can convert into equity in distress. Optiver, meanwhile, was seeking about $700 million of debt and a $200 million revolver to expand trading. People familiar with the plans said market uncertainty and the U.S. midterms left timing unsettled and the financing could still be abandoned.

Municipal borrowing continued for specific expansion projects. The Villages plans almost $180 million of unrated high-yield debt, expected to price October 20, to fund 3,860 homes and amenities including 27 holes of championship golf. It follows about $127 million borrowed last year for the first phase of a roughly 6,670-unit expansion.

The Las Vegas Valley Water District plans about $580 million of tax-exempt debt this week for infrastructure and refunding. Projects include water supply for the Apex Industrial Park, a Henderson pipeline and participation in Southern California recycling. S&P rated the bonds AA+, citing successful water conservation and banked supplies despite customer growth. The district is also suing over a federal policy that could reduce Nevada's Colorado River allocation by as much as 70% in the worst conditions; the river supplies about 90% of the valley's water.

BofA's Kay Hope supplied a new assessment of African corporate funding. Hard-currency issuance reached $13.3 billion in the first nine months, including $3.25 billion of private placements, the fastest pace since 2021's $17 billion. Issuers came from 11 countries, against eight in 2021. Hope cited more upgrades than downgrades and no sector payment defaults since 2020, while warning that sovereign stress could still reach companies.

The maturity schedule makes continued access consequential. United Bank for Africa has $300 million due next month, followed by $2.2 billion across four issuers in 2027 and nearly $7 billion across nine in 2028. The latter includes Eskom's $1.5 billion, Tullow Oil's $1.2 billion and Transnet's $1 billion. Hope expects annual supply of $8 billion-$12 billion, though high rates may redirect some refinancing toward local markets, loans or Gulf funding.

## AI Financing Debate Gains New Contract Economics

CoreWeave failed to sustain Monday's early equity recovery despite a Goldman Sachs upgrade. Its shares rose as much as 7.4%, briefly fell more than 2% and finished 0.4% lower. Analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded the stock to buy but reduced her target to $106 from $139, acknowledging uncertainty over the availability and cost of the next phase of financing.

Her analysis estimated that CoreWeave's blended debt cost could increase 100-200 basis points, but probably not more, leaving equity returns attractive in Goldman's assessment. Borges expects tight computing supply and CoreWeave's performance and execution advantages to support project returns over the next 24 months. The judgment concerned future financing economics amid current stress, rather than a recovery in its bond prices.

A Friday JPMorgan analysis reported Monday provided a more detailed contractual counterargument to the market's concerns. Analysts including Samik Chatterjee estimated a typical five-year contract's unlevered internal rate of return in the mid-teens, above an estimated blended cost of capital of 9%-11%. Take-or-pay commitments secure customers before capacity becomes operational, with possible additional proceeds from contracting GPUs again after the initial five years.

In the bank's conservative scenario, capital expenditure consumes about 51% of a contract's value, with roughly 80% of that investment financed through asset-level debt. After debt repayment, cash equal to about 16% of the contract value could remain, sufficient in its model to cover roughly five years of data-center obligations without renewing the customer contract. The denominator is contract value, not a projected recovery percentage for CoreWeave's corporate bondholders.

The same analysis identified why favorable project returns can coexist with large financing needs. A fully operational gigawatt could generate $10 billion-$15 billion of annual revenue, while adding that capacity requires more than $35 billion upfront. JPMorgan estimates that existing operations may not fund expansion until 2030, when installed operating capacity could reach four to five times annual additions. The balance between cash-producing capacity and construction therefore determines how long external funding remains necessary.

Nscale added a prospective demand commitment to that debate. The Nvidia-backed developer is discussing a computing-power agreement with Anthropic potentially worth almost $45 billion, involving 460 megawatts at a new West Virginia center using Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips. At the same time, investors have challenged the roughly $30 billion valuation sought for its IPO, with some suggesting $16 billion-$19 billion would attract more support. The proposed customer business and resistance to its equity valuation describe different parts of the same funding challenge.

GTCR's Nelson Iginla offered a separate view from software acquisition finance. He said lenders provided a strong package for the CCC Intelligent Solutions buyout because of the quality of the business. Proprietary data and the network connecting insurers, repair shops and other participants make its services difficult to reproduce, in his assessment. But GTCR has also examined businesses where AI is already eroding financial performance. His distinction was company-specific resilience rather than a general restoration of financing appetite across software.

New IMF research extended the AI debate beyond capital spending. A working paper drawing on more than 700 million online job postings across 110 economies found hiring in exposed industries had declined nearly 10% since ChatGPT's late-2022 release. The decline was leveling off as demand grew for workers able to use AI. Larger firms were more likely to request those skills, although fewer than 20% appeared to make them a requirement even in that group.

Pan Gongsheng described a related sequencing problem for monetary policy: AI could increase investment and inflation in the short run before raising productivity and reducing price growth over the medium to long term. He said aggregate employment had not yet been significantly affected, although job structures were changing. His aggregate assessment and the IMF's findings for exposed industries concern different measures of the adjustment, with new hiring opportunities beginning to emerge alongside displacement.

## Forward Market Significance

U.S. housing data on October 20 will put actual construction and transactions beside the deterioration in builder confidence. September starts are expected at 1.31 million after 1.275 million, while preliminary permits are expected at 1.40 million after 1.403 million. Pending home sales are expected to fall 0.5% month on month after a 0.3% increase. A rebound in starts alongside weak transactions would leave a different inventory and cash-flow problem for builders than a simultaneous contraction in both.

Weekly ADP employment change arrives Tuesday, followed by mortgage applications Wednesday and initial jobless claims Thursday. Friday's preliminary October S&P Global manufacturing and services PMIs will offer a broader activity comparison: consensus expects 55.5 and 57.9, respectively, against previous readings of 55.9 and 58.8. Final Michigan figures the same day are expected to put five-year inflation expectations at 3.5%. The combination will bear on whether high financing costs are slowing demand while inflation expectations remain difficult to contain.

Treasury's 20-year auction on October 21 and five-year TIPS auction October 22 will test demand for long nominal exposure and inflation protection after Monday's real-yield increase. The question is how readily buyers absorb duration at higher yields while large corporate borrowers are also raising funds. Those are upcoming sales, distinct from the primary corporate transactions already completed.

France's Friday Moody's review approaches with a larger yield penalty and continuing political resistance to fiscal adjustment. Britain's Wednesday inflation report, forecast at 3.4% for September, precedes the October 28 budget and a potential November BOE increase. Canada's October 28 decision now carries a sharper disagreement between the softer core-price evidence and survey signals of future pass-through, with several major banks having moved to a hike forecast.

Bank Indonesia's Wednesday decision comes after another leg of losses in stocks, bonds and the rupiah, making stabilization and the response to prospective benchmark outflows immediate policy issues. Japan's Friday inflation release and Australia's coming inflation data will help establish whether their different official emphases on normalization and labor-market restraint persist.

Meta and Tesla's Wednesday earnings will test the operating assumptions behind Monday's technology recovery. For AI creditors, revenue conversion, construction spending and the cost of fresh financing remain linked but distinct questions. Nscale's negotiations and proposed IPO will show whether a large potential customer commitment can translate into acceptable funding terms, while CoreWeave's capacity ramp continues to determine its dependence on external capital. China's promised guidance on loan and bond benchmarks will separately establish how the proposed overnight policy framework reaches actual financing contracts.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries fall as technology rebounds, corporate supply returns and French debt sells off
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries fell on October 19 as recovering technology shares reduced demand for safety, corporate borrowers returned and French debt added to global yield pressure. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 6.69 basis points to 5.1397%, with the real yield up 6.1 basis points to 2.783% and breakeven inflation up just 0.59 basis point to 2.3567%. The 2-year yield rose 6.36 basis points to 4.7719%; intermediate maturities sold off more than the very long end. The reversal only partly unwound the preceding rally: 10-year yields remained 9.81 basis points lower over the week.

The Nasdaq 100 recovered 1.17%, but improved risk appetite did not extend evenly across financing markets. Walmart and Kimberly-Clark completed large dollar offerings, while U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads tightened modestly. A $175 million Manhattan office securitization was postponed. Homebuilder confidence fell to 29, its lowest since June 2012, as expensive mortgages and construction costs constrained demand.

France's fiscal tensions intensified after violent cost-of-living protests; its 10-year yield rose about 14 basis points to nearly 4.95% during the session, ahead of Friday's Moody's review. In Canada, softer-than-expected CPI gave way to concern about rising inflation expectations and planned price increases, strengthening October hike bets and sending bonds lower. China reported stronger growth and proposed an overnight policy-rate framework, while Indonesia's benchmark-reclassification threat spread into government debt and the rupiah.
overall_summary.summary: Higher real yields drove most of the Treasury reversal despite a 14-year low in homebuilder confidence, while strong demand for large corporate offerings coexisted with modestly wider investment-grade spreads and stalled property financing.
